env.#1: Resource identifier of THIS application - the "aud" the authorization server mints its tokens for.
env.#2: Key set of the issuing authorization server, used to verify the token signature.
env.#4: Optional. Only set these when the matching option is enabled in packages/suissetec_mcp_auth.yaml:

post-install-output: * Set <info>SUISSETEC_MCP_AUDIENCE</info> (this application's resource identifier) and <info>SUISSETEC_MCP_JWKS_URI</info> (the issuer's key set).
* This bundle brings <comment>no firewall of its own</comment> - add a stateless one in <info>config/packages/security.yaml</info>:

* <fg=red>Firewall order matters.</> Symfony uses the FIRST firewall whose pattern matches. In <comment>Sylius</comment> the mcp firewall must sit <comment>ABOVE</comment> the admin and shop firewalls - their regexes (<info>%sylius.security.admin_regex%</info> / <info>%sylius.security.shop_regex%</info>) are broad enough to swallow <info>/mcp</info>, and then the path is never reachable.

* <comment>issuer</comment> is intentionally left unset in the shipped configuration: today's tokens carry no <info>iss</info> claim, and configuring an issuer makes that claim mandatory - every real token would be refused. Enable it only against an issuer that sets it.
* Add the key-set warm-up to your deployment, after the cache clear, so the first request after a release does not pay for the fetch: <info>bin/console suissetec:mcp-auth:warm-jwks</info>

* Inherit the shipped contract test (<info>Suissetec\McpAuthBundle\Test\McpAuthContractTestCase</info>) in <comment>tests/</comment> and feed it this application's own configuration values - it runs the whole token-verification contract against your setup.
* Enforce permissions where the tool runs (<info>#[IsGranted]</info>). Hiding a tool from a listing is comfort, not access control.
* MCP logs are written to <comment>var/log/suissetec_mcp_auth-YYYY-MM.log</comment> (monthly rotation, 3 months retention). Requires <info>symfony/monolog-bundle</info>.
